summary: Realtime Console 'Usage Snapshot' shows inflated tokens after editing query filters
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that the Console "Usage Snapshot" card for a workspace displays a token count that is consistently ~2x the token count shown by the raw usage export after they edit a saved query's filters (timespan and org filter).

Impact:
- Customer cannot reconcile near-real-time usage with raw exports — blocks weekly reconciliation and alerts.
- Affects billing visibility and trust for dedicated customers using committed capacity.
- Reported by ScaleWave (dedicated) for us-east-1 workspace; they see the discrepancy within 1–3 minutes after editing queries.

Environment:
- Console (web) in prod: us-east-1
- Workspace: scalewave-prod (dedicated cluster)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to Console as an owner of a dedicated workspace (ScaleWave account).
2) Open Usage -> Realtime -> Usage Snapshot (top-right card).
3) Click 'Edit query' and change timespan from '1h' to '24h' and toggle Organization filter (e.g., include/exclude a sub-org).
4) Save query. Observe Usage Snapshot token value (updates within 1–3 minutes).
5) Export raw usage CSV for the same timespan and filters. Compare token totals — snapshot value is inflated compared to CSV export.
expected_behavior: Usage Snapshot should reflect the same token totals as the raw export for equivalent time window and filters (subject to reasonable real-time lag < 2 minutes).
actual_behavior: After editing and saving a query, the Usage Snapshot shows a token total 1.5–3x higher than the raw export for the same filters. The discrepancy resolves only after manually refreshing the console page or waiting ~20–30 minutes.
logs_observed: Frontend: console-logs show 'snapshot:cached=true' after save; API: /api/usage/snapshot returns X tokens while /api/usage/raw-export returns Y tokens (Y < X). Cache-service logs show repeated 'cache-miss' then 'cache-set' events for the snapshot key; keys contain timespan but not query filter hash in some runs. Relevant trace id: trace-20260310-8872 (linked to tracing-hook SUP-10721-TR).
workaround: Manual page refresh or navigate away and back to Realtime page forces a fresh snapshot read and reconciles numbers. As a temporary customer-facing workaround, instruct ScaleWave to refresh the page after editing queries.
comments: Support (2026-03-10 09:12 UTC) - Amara: Acknowledged. Reproduced in production with ScaleWave account. First-response sent to customer with temporary refresh workaround.
Customer (2026-03-10 09:28 UTC) - Elena (ScaleWave): Confirmed refresh fixes numbers but process is not acceptable for our automated dashboards. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.

SRE (2026-03-10 12:04 UTC) - Diego: Initial hypothesis: snapshot cache key missing query filter hash; after edit save we set cache 'stale' flag but UI still serves cached snapshot if cache contains an entry for the timespan-only key. Creating reproducer script and capturing cache keys. Linked trace: trace-20260310-8872.

Frontend (2026-03-11 08:15 UTC) - Priya: Found commit that changed caching behavior (console: cache-key-generation: include timespan but excluded filterMap due to payload size optimization). Will prepare PR to include a stable short hash of filterMap in cache key.
investigation_notes: Cached snapshot keys sampled: 'snapshot:workspace:us-east-1:timespan=24h' (missing filter hash) in ~40% of reproductions.
When cache key omitted filter hash, snapshot returned aggregate for entire workspace (overcounting), while raw export pipeline used full filter set, hence lower counts.
Trace shows race: UI saves query -> backend returns 'ok' -> UI requests snapshot using previous cache key until local cache invalidation completes.

Reproducer: automated E2E script toggling filter produce inflated snapshot in 6/10 runs; adding a 200ms delay after save reduces incidence to 0/10, suggesting timing/race between save and cache invalidation.
Relevant code area: console/src/services/usageSnapshot.ts (cache key builder), cache-service redis namespace 'console:snapshot'.
resolution: Workaround provided (manual refresh). Fix planned: include deterministic short hash of query filters in snapshot cache key and add server-side validation to ignore stale keys when query version != cache.version. Frontend PR #842 prepared; backend cache-service patch to follow. Target hotfix deploy to staging 2026-03-13 and prod rollout 2026-03-16. Post-deploy, run reconciliation smoke test and notify ScaleWave.
